filament.name: Bambu PLA Basic Orange + Bambu PLA Glow Green

datums.A: Stator bottom (primary). Print bed for the stand.

fits_mm.running_rollers: +0.40 diametral PLA-on-PLA for parts printed separately and assembled (rollers on both races). Slicer XY hole compensation stays 0.
fits_mm.top_load_slots: Slot width = roller Ø + running + 2 nozzles. Drop in from above. No support. This kit does not PIP the rollers — a lying OD prints as layers.
fits_mm.slip_retainer: +0.28 diametral D-hole in the snap groove. Clocked to one orientation. C-gap lets the clip flex over the constant journal and seat in the undercut.
fits_mm.no_rotor_rub: C-clip sits in the journal groove, 0.20 above the plate. It is not a running face on the turbine.
fits_mm.thrust_land: One stator: thin Y-frame + race ring + open fence + constant journal. Thin flat thrust under the blade roots: the race ring is the lower land (not a cookie disk), plate underside is the upper land, radial-axis rollers between (pack height = roller Ø, 0.20 float each land). The pack outer land must reach the blade radius so the thin plate is not a cantilever. Inner and outer keeper walls stay after the top-load cut so rollers cannot slide out the open Y-frame. Fence sits on the race ring and is looser than the plate bore (spacer, not a journal). Journal pass Ø is smaller than the plate bore so the rotor drops on. Do not print a fat shoulder or bead above the plate.
fits_mm.do_not_nest_cup_pip: Do not print the plate around the rollers on the bed. Race-to-roller at +0.40 is 0.10 mm/side — they fuse. Print rollers standing. Drop them into the top-load slots, then drop the rotor over the journal, then snap the C-clip into the groove. Radial capture is the keeper walls. Axial capture is the race + clocked C-clip, not a top lip and not a rubbing washer.

lessons.title: Start from a blank document
lessons.teach: cad_new_project first. solid_scene must show 0 bodies before the first extrude. Do not continue a recovered or older Print Kit Tutor (tan nest, red disc, leftover helix planes). Hide construction planes and finished loft sketches before save so File → Open is the merged-stator kit, not orange datums.

lessons.title: Fits are per role and material
lessons.teach: Fits are per role *and* per whether the parts share a plate. Assembled running (rollers on races) is +0.40 because those parts print as other bodies. Top-load slots add two nozzles so rollers drop in from above without support. Same-plate PIP is +0.80 — do not PIP a lying roller (the OD is layers). The journal is a constant pass Ø smaller than the plate bore so the rotor drops on. Clocked C-clip uses slip +0.28 in an undercut groove 0.20 above the plate — it must not rub the rotor. Pull the C-gap to remove. Model 0.20 axial float at every running land. Fence height is below pack height so rollers touch both races. Fence ID is looser than the plate bore. Keeper walls inboard and outboard of each roller survive the top-load cut so the pack cannot slide into the Y-frame. Do not nest the plate around the rollers on the bed.

lessons.title: Snug is not a press
lessons.teach: FDM press fits fail from elephant foot. The plate bore is running, not friction. A fat shoulder or snap bead above the plate blocks assembly — the rotor cannot drop on. Keep the journal a constant pass Ø. Retain with a clocked C-clip that snaps into an undercut groove and pulls off at the C-gap. Functional lands start above a 2-nozzle lead-in on every bed-printed bore. No metal 608s. No inward top lip over the rollers. Plastics are PLA Basic Orange and PLA Glow Green only.

lessons.title: Individual parts, then an assembly
lessons.teach: Each body that moves is its own component with exactly one occurrence. assembly_create_component already inserts the root instance — do not create a second copy. Ground the one stator. Revolute the plate bore on the short journal about Z, and each roller about its radial axis — never a blade-spar face, never a standing-Z puck axis. rotor_spin is plate bore ↔ journal. Rigid retainer_sit in the journal groove. There is no separate axle puck, cage disk, or bushing. Blades stay one printed body with the plate. Drop rollers into the top-load slots, drop the rotor over the journal, then snap the C-clip into the groove. Do not claim a pickup cartridge.

lessons.title: Print a thin flat thrust that takes rotation about Z
lessons.teach: A tall skinny sleeve cannot hold aero loads at the blade tips. A tall drum with webs climbing the wall is the same mistake in orange. Matching 8 mm flats is still a pancake stack. Two separate flats (axle disk + cage disk) are extra plastic. Standing-Z pucks slide on their end faces — that is not rolling under −Z. An inboard pack at ~58% of the plate leaves the blade roots cantilevered on a thin plate — the couple never reaches the race. Use a **thin flat thrust** on **one stator**: ≥6 cylinders, axis **radial** (e_r), diameter = pack height (min Ø8), on a large PCD **under the blade roots**. Relative motion at the race is circumferential; a tangent axis would roll inward/outward. The stator race is the lower land; the plate underside is the upper land; a short journal only centers. The plate bore is the radial land; the fence ID must be looser. Overturning is a couple across that disk, not a tall land. Print rollers standing (circular layers); drop them into top-load slots. Do not PIP a lying roller. Radial capture is inner/outer keeper walls that survive the top-load cut — no bars over the pack. Axial capture is the race + clocked C-snap.

lessons.title: Keep the machine even
lessons.teach: Three helical blades at 120°. Root azimuth 30° so a 60° helix stays balanced. The merged stator is grounded — the plate freewheels on the thin thrust pack. An odd one-sided vane is not a turbine.

lessons.title: Blades and hub are one part
lessons.teach: The rotor is a single printed body: a thin root plate (print sit + upper thrust race, floor 3.2 mm) and helical blades that end on that sit plane. Through-plate stump is the sit-plane chord. Above the plate, treat the join organically: first loft station is a fatter airfoil on the plate top, then the helix. The tip keeps a flat landing (last loft section is planar) with a short chord taper into that face. No rectangular print arms or spars. Do not grow a tall drum or moment webs on the plate — overturning is taken by the wide thrust pack **under the blade roots**. Print standing on the plate. Drop rollers into the stator slots, then the rotor on the pack.

lessons.title: The section is a 2026-appropriate airfoil
lessons.teach: Directionless VAWTs see reversing α. Build the low-TSR symmetric section NACA 0024-4.5/3.5 (t/c 24%, xt/c 35%, LE index 4.5, blunt TE ≥ 2 nozzles). Organic roots are appearance only. Draft the chord (root > tip) so the standing print needs little support.

lessons.title: Scale is a parameter; 1.0 fills an X2D
lessons.teach: Linear dimensions are the X2D-max design (256×256×260, 8 mm margin). spec.scale shrinks the source (exam default 0.4). Feature sizes that would go below printable (roller Ø8, roller length 8, TE 0.8, 4-nozzle walls, plate 3.2 mm, base 3.2 mm) are clamped. Pack height is the roller diameter, not a 3.2 mm standing puck. noBS-CAD has no document-level scale feature yet — the spec parameter is the source of truth.

lessons.title: Print rotational parts lying down
lessons.teach: Never design a tall skinny shaft that needs a tower of support. The stator prints flat: thin Y-frame, race ring with keeper walls, open fence, journal. Retainer prints flat. Rollers print standing (axis Z, circular layers) and drop into top-load slots (axis radial). The rotor stands on a thin root plate so each blade ends on that flat horizontal, with an organic blend on the top face. The plate is not nested around the rollers on the bed. Do not print a separate axle disk and cage disk.

lessons.title: Helical blades, not a straight fence
lessons.teach: A prismatic extrusion is idle for most of the rev. Loft a closed NACA at ≥2 stations with ≥45° helix. Mid-chord stays on R. Chord stays tangent. Open tips — no end cap. First loft station above the plate is an organic fatter root; the last station is a smaller chord that still ends on a flat landing.

lessons.title: Ship an assembly drawing
lessons.teach: Create a drawing sheet, auto-layout standard views, and annotate fits, scale, print orientation, and the BOM. A kit without a drawing is not a product.

lessons.title: Publish the design report
lessons.teach: Write the iteration log, airfoil/Re, role-based fits, roller pack, scale vs X2D, finish, BOM, and plastic cost. READY TO PRINT without a costed report is a fail.

lessons.title: Export one laid-out plate
lessons.teach: Wipe Print-Kit-Tutor/ first so leftover five-plate and shaft/hub/wings names are gone. Save the assembled .nbcad, then solid_move_copy parts onto the bed (rotor standing on the deck, others flat) and solid_export_3mf once as 01-kit. Two materials only: PLA Orange and PLA Glow (rotor). Do not export the assembled nest as the print job.
